blindSummary:
This state/province recorded the highest transfeminicide toll in the country in 2024 — 17 LGBT+ homicides, of which 11 were trans women — and remains among the highest-count states/provinces in 2025. The raw violence data is a negative signal for a visitor, though part of the elevated count reflects its superior reporting infrastructure rather than proportionally higher danger.

Counterbalanced by the strongest institutional response of any state/province in the country: transfeminicide was made a distinct crime in July 2024 under a law named for a murdered trans woman; a dedicated transfeminicide investigation unit was created in December 2024 with mandatory 72h/48h action protocols under a 2025 attorney-general agreement; and a new gender-police unit with 30 patrol units launched in August 2025. Legal gender recognition has existed here since 2014, extended to 12-year-olds by a 2021 decree. For a visitor assaulted in this state/province there is trained machinery to investigate; in other, weaker-resourced neighbouring states/provinces there is none.

Modestly above the national average: the protective and investigative framework is the strongest in the country and materially changes what a visitor who encounters violence or discrimination faces after the fact, even though the pre-violence risk data is the country's worst.
